name: Roofing, residential
description: Architectural asphalt shingles with underlayment, drip edge, starter and nails; tear-off; ice barrier at eaves; ridge and hip cap with ridge vent; valleys; step flashing; pipe boots; standing-seam metal panels. Use the pitch on the item so areas are true roof surfaces. Assemblies only: set your own rates.
author: CadCraft

sources.title: International Residential Code, Section R905 Requirements for Roof Coverings (asphalt shingles, underlayment, drip edge)
The NRCA Roofing Manual (Membrane Roof Systems; Steep-slope Roof Systems)
Plain geometry: the quantity follows from the measured length, height or area and the stated module (no outside source needed)
International Residential Code, Section R806 Roof Ventilation
The product data sheet of the coating, adhesive or product you specify (spread rate, coverage, coats)
International Building Code, Chapter 15 Roof Assemblies and Rooftop Structures, Section 1507 Requirements for Roof Coverings

assume: Shingles: 3 bundles per square of 100 SF (most architectural and three-tab shingles; check the wrapper), 10% waste for hips, valleys and starter cuts.
Synthetic underlayment over the whole deck (IRC R905.1.1), 10% for laps.
Drip edge at eaves and rakes (IRC R905.2.8.5): the plane’s whole outline P, in 10 ft lengths; lower it where planes meet hips and valleys.
Starter strip along eaves and rakes: P.
Nails: about 320 per square (4 per shingle, IRC R905.2.6 minimum; 6 in high-wind areas).
items.note: Measure each roof plane on the plan and give the item the roof pitch (Roofs and slopes): A is then the sloped surface; P is the plane’s outline.

assume: Standing-seam panels 16 in wide, 10% waste.
Clips at 24 in along each seam: 16 / 12 x 2 = 2.67 SF per clip, so 0.375 clips per SF (spacing is set by the panel maker and the wind design).
High-temperature underlayment over the whole deck, 10% for laps.
Eave and rake trim on the outline P.
items.note: Measure each roof plane on the plan and give the item the roof pitch (Roofs and slopes): A is then the sloped surface; P is the plane’s outline.
